name: zombie-run
intent: In-place zombie run cycle with a slightly hunched torso, knees kept bent, and alternating leg lifts and lowers; both arms remain loose and swing asymmetrically, creating an uneven running rhythm.

phases.name: rise-and-first-leg-lift
phases.description: The body rises and the first leg moves into a lifted step; the hips reach their peak along the Z axis at f5.

phases.name: lower-and-mid-cycle-compression
phases.description: The body lowers and compresses through the middle of the cycle; the hips reach their lowest position along the Z axis at f12.

phases.name: second-rise-with-opposite-leg
phases.description: The body rises a second time with the opposite leg; the second lift peak occurs at f17.

phases.name: second-lower-and-loop-return
phases.description: The body lowers and compresses a second time, then returns to the loop-start pose; f24 is near f0.

keyPoses.description: Peak of the first step; one leg is lifted and the hips are highest along the Z axis.
Mid-cycle compression; the hips are lowest along the Z axis.
Peak step with the opposite leg.
Second compression before returning to the start of the loop.

weightTransfer.description: The hips shift along +X from the start of the loop to a maximum around f14, then return near the initial position by f24; at the same time, there are two rise-compression pulses along Z. The two legs alternate lifting across the two half-steps.
weightTransfer.contactCaveat: The evidence is not sufficient to assign the exact support leg or the exact timing of ground contact.

bodyMechanics.description: The coordination sequence is compression → first leg lifts as the hips rise → mid-cycle compression → opposite leg lifts → return to the loop. The upper torso and shoulders sway across the two half-steps; both arms swing loosely and change configuration correspondingly.
